about: The Tour (shell/tour.js): each slide plays a title card, then its steps on the before tree, then on the after tree (once per option). Steps are the harness's step runner (runtime/steps.ts) plus the paced ones in runtime/tour.ts: hover (draws the element's tooltip), highlight (after only unless both), scroll, typeSlow, selectLine, hold. open: the scenario's own open steps, played paced (default), fast, or skip. beforeSide / afterSide override scenario, steps or open per side; options replace the after pass; surface phone plays pages (one scenario each).

slides.title: Settings in six sections
slides.caption: One short page — Models, Keys, Voice, Box, Safety, Appearance — instead of a long scroll of every knob. Key sync, mission host, schedules and sync intervals leave the UI.

slides.title: Models: one picker per role
slides.caption: Chat, Background and Voice each get one picker from the live OpenRouter list. There is no Images & PDFs row: images and PDFs go to the Chat model, and only if it can't read them to a built-in vision model.

slides.title: What each model can do — pick a layout
slides.caption: A small capability view for the models your roles use: tools, images, PDFs, caching, helpers, and where we know it from (learned on the box, the catalog, or untested). Three layouts are built; pick one.

options.label: Option A — a table under the pickers
Option B — one line under each picker
Option C — folded into one Capabilities row

slides.title: Keys, trimmed
slides.caption: OpenRouter first, then the service keys you actually use; the other providers fold away with a count of how many are set.

slides.title: The Box section
slides.caption: Everything about the box in one place: where it is and whether this vault syncs to it. Sync intervals and the key-sync blurb are gone.

slides.title: The context dial counts cached tokens once
slides.caption: On a long cached chat the dial used to add the cached tokens on top of the prompt and read about twice the real size. Now it shows the real number against the model's real window.

slides.title: The dial is there when you reopen a chat
slides.caption: Before, the dial only appeared after you sent something. Now a reopened chat shows the context its last turn reported.

slides.title: Near the limit of a 1M-window model
slides.caption: At 880k the dial is red against Sonnet 5.5's real 1M window, and the tooltip says the next message first summarizes the earlier conversation. Before, it was pegged against a fixed 200k.

slides.title: A small-window model
slides.caption: Qwen3 32B has a 131k window: at 120k the dial is red and the next message compacts first, so the prompt fits. Before, it looked amber against an assumed 200k and the next prompt would be rejected.

slides.title: Compaction is a divider, not a disappearance
slides.caption: When a long chat is summarized, nothing leaves the transcript: a quiet divider sits above the messages kept word for word and opens to the summary. Before, the earlier messages vanished behind a banner.

slides.title: Ctrl+K and Ctrl+L say which model they use
slides.caption: Ctrl+L (ask) and Ctrl+K (edit) now say which model they run on, chosen by role instead of whatever the chat pane happens to be on. Which role each uses is your call — three options are built.

options.label: Option A — Ctrl+K and Ctrl+L on Chat
Option B — Ctrl+K on Background, Ctrl+L on Chat (default)
Option C — Ctrl+K and Ctrl+L on Background

slides.title: Ctrl+L works when the chat model is Auto
slides.caption: With the chat pane on Auto, Ctrl+L used to fail with “No API key for auto”. Now it resolves Auto the way a chat turn does and answers.

slides.title: The PDF tool reads by page range
slides.caption: Asked about a 320-page PDF, the tool returns pages 1–3 and says how many pages there are; the model asks for the range it needs. Before, every call extracted the whole PDF and dumped ~60k characters into the chat.

slides.title: Notes search finds what a row shows
slides.caption: “failure modes” is in a note's title. Now the search matches the title, highlighted text and summary, in any word order, and the count leaves out cleared notes.

slides.title: @-mentions rank names that start with what you typed
slides.caption: A long file name that starts with “eigengap” used to sink below short names that merely contain it. Now: name starts with, then name contains, then path.

slides.title: The phone page, rebuilt in React — identical
slides.caption: The phone app is now a bundled React + TypeScript app instead of one big HTML file with in-browser Babel. It should look exactly the same: watch the same pages before and after.

slides.title: Chat runs on the box — and says so when it can't
slides.caption: With a box configured, every chat turn runs on the box. When the box can't be reached, the composer is disabled and says why, instead of quietly running the agent on the laptop.

steps.label: Box unreachable — agent runs on the box

slides.title: Not in the tour yet, and what's yours to decide

sections.title: Your decisions
items: Capability view: option A (table), B (one line per picker) or C (folded)
Ctrl+K / Ctrl+L roles: A (both Chat), B (K Background, L Chat — default) or C (both Background)
Built-in vision model for images the Chat model can't read: Gemini 3.5 Flash (no setting)
